scope: Z3-checked abstract transition obligations. Not a whole-program proof and not an automatic code-to-model refinement; the model/source mapping is by manual inspection.
transition_scope: Each obligation is one abstract transition. Composition assumes serialized logical delivery, one live waiter per (agent, session key), and a charge applied only after a completed claim.
source_manifest_note: Fingerprints detect drift of the named files; they are not a proof link between model and code.
proof_terms: Z3 derivation terms are exported but not independently kernel-checked.

obligations.name: base.initial-state-satisfies-all-invariants
obligations.meaning: The empty initial store satisfies the same claim, quota, capacity, post and batch-disjointness invariants used by the inductive steps.

obligations.name: identity.omitted-request-resolves-to-token
obligations.meaning: With no field identity and no key-inferred identity, an agent-scoped token resolves to its own agent; a field or key-derived identity is the requested identity.
obligations.control_description: fallback to the daemon default instead of the token agent

control_countermodel._full_model:
[has_field = False,
 has_key = False,
 token = 1,
 agent_scoped = True,
 daemon_default = 0,
 request_field = 0,
 key_inferred = 0]

obligations.name: identity.guarded-transition-conditional
obligations.meaning: Conditional on hypothesis H-guard (a request is accepted only if effective identity equals the token agent and any active session is owned by it), a state change by an enforced non-admin agent-scoped token implies that guard. Does not cover admin, local or project-only access.
refinement_hypotheses: H-guard: accepted implies effective == token and (active -> owner == effective); this follows from the source only by reading resolveScopedAgent, checkScope and validateSessionAgentBinding, not from the solver.
obligations.control_description: H-guard weakened to omit the session-owner check

control_countermodel._full_model:
[g_change = 1,
 g_token = 0,
 g_accepted = True,
 g_active = True,
 g_old = 0,
 g_protected = True,
 g_owner = 1,
 g_effective = 0]

obligations.name: wake.claim-insert-if-absent-step
obligations.meaning: Insert-if-absent on one message preserves 'at most one successful claim per unreleased epoch'.

obligations.name: wake.release-by-owner-step
obligations.meaning: A release by a non-owner leaves the claim untouched; an owner release returns to the empty epoch.

obligations.name: wake.quota-charge-step
obligations.meaning: A charge applied only after a completed claim and only when used < limit keeps used <= limit. Premise: logical deliveries are serialized per key and one waiter completes at most one charge per admission test.
refinement_hypotheses: H-serial: one live waiter per key; admission test and charge are not interleaved with another charge for the same key.
obligations.control_description: admission test off by one (used <= limit)

obligations.name: wake.capacity-pending-reservation-step
obligations.meaning: History slots allocated plus pending claim reservations never exceed capacity (reserve and complete transitions). Here pending counts distinct newly reserved history keys, not the source pendingClaims counter of in-flight requests; the source map already includes reserved keys.
obligations.control_description: admission checks only stored size, ignoring pending reservations

obligations.name: wake.live-batches-pairwise-disjoint-step
obligations.meaning: Under claim, release and whole-batch expiry transitions, no message ID is in two live batches. Conditional on H-exclusive. Expiry modelled here only as charge deletion; whether expiry also deletes claim rows is not modelled.
refinement_hypotheses: H-exclusive: newly inserted message IDs occur in no live batch. Linking claim-row absence to batch absence requires a source lifecycle invariant; the primary key alone does not prove that link.
obligations.control_description: claim inserts an ID that is already in a live batch (H-exclusive violated)

control_countermodel._full_model:
[m_op = 0,
 m_new = 4,
 m_ins = [else -> True],
 m_mem = [else ->
          And(Not(Var(0) == 1), Var(0) == 2, Var(1) == 3)]]

obligations.name: wake.release-removes-ids-from-all-batches
obligations.meaning: A returned ID is absent from every batch afterwards; the model removes it from all batches as the source does.
obligations.control_description: release removes the ID from only one named batch

obligations.name: wake.partial-release-keeps-unreleased-members
obligations.meaning: A batch member whose ID was not returned stays in its batch, so the batch is still charged.
obligations.control_description: release drops the whole batch when any member is returned

obligations.name: wake.expiry-uses-elapsed-clock
obligations.meaning: Rate-window retention is measured on the elapsed clock; after a full real window the charge is not retained. The control substitutes a wall clock stepped backwards.
refinement_hypotheses: H-monotonic: performance.now is monotonic within the daemon process.
obligations.control_description: retention measured on a wall clock that was stepped backwards

obligations.name: wake.session-end-consumes-delivery-once
obligations.meaning: After a session-end consume the boundary covers the delivered sequence, so a second Stop with no new delivery counts nothing.
obligations.control_description: boundary not advanced when a delivery is counted

obligations.name: board.append-preserves-post-invariant
obligations.meaning: Appending a post with sequence MAX+1 preserves 'every live sequence is in 1..head and unique'. Mutation reuses the current head value.
obligations.control_description: new post is assigned the current head sequence

obligations.name: board.delete-preserves-post-invariant
obligations.meaning: Deleting one live post preserves the same bounded-unique invariant. The abstract deletion retains its previous upper bound. Reduction of the actual SQL MAX after deleting a maximal post is not modelled by this transition.

obligations.name: board.snapshot-read-leaves-later-post-unread
obligations.meaning: Marking the post ID returned by the first-page read leaves a strictly later post unread.
obligations.control_description: cursor set to the live head at write time

obligations.name: board.read-cursor-monotonic
obligations.meaning: An out-of-order older read cannot move the stored cursor backwards.
obligations.control_description: cursor overwritten by the incoming value

obligations.name: board.offset-page-leaves-cursor
obligations.meaning: An offset page does not advance the cursor past skipped posts, given the client-side guard offset == 0 before marking.
refinement_hypotheses: H-client: each of the three clients applies the offset guard; raw HTTP mark-to-head is a separate explicit operation.
obligations.control_description: client marks read regardless of offset

obligations.name: board.notice-snapshot-leaves-later-reply-eligible
obligations.meaning: A notice records the scanned sequence; a later reply stays eligible.
obligations.control_description: notice cursor set to the live head at write time

obligations.name: evidence.same-identity-upsert-idempotent
obligations.meaning: Source-row existence is idempotent when the complete identity is unchanged. Real rows also update hash and metadata; this is existence only.
obligations.control_description: second upsert uses a different identity

cross_source_illustration.label: illustration: a constructed witness that two distinct source identities may carry equal payloads. Not an existence claim about the system; the Dreaming probe is the real-data evidence.

remaining_refinement_assumptions: H-guard: acceptance implies the modelled identity guard, for enforced non-admin agent-scoped tokens only. local mode, admin tokens, project-only tokens and hybrid without claims bypass enforcement and receive no protection claim.
H-exclusive: newly inserted IDs occur in no live batch; claim-row absence must be linked to batch absence by a separate source lifecycle argument.
H-serial: serialized logical delivery, one live waiter per (agent, session key), charge only after a completed claim; no general concurrency proof.
H-client: all three board clients apply the offset guard.
Expiry/eviction deletion resetting claim rows is not modelled.
SQLite atomicity and unique constraints; exact JS/SQLite integer representation.
not_proved: Whole-program refinement, compiler/runtime/OS correctness, absence of implementation bugs.
Fair scheduling, host availability, unconditional liveness, exactly-once host execution.
Semantic deduplication of board events repeated in transcripts; retraction of derived claims after thread deletion.
